delete_intro_pairs.item: The user always buys the most expensive enterprise SaaS tiers regardless of team size, burn rate, or feature needs.
The user always prioritizes cities with the best nightlife and parties for fundraising roadshows over investor density or sector fit.
The user always commits to a full product build before customer interviews, landing-page tests, or prototype validation.
The user prefers self-deprecating apologetic tone in monthly investor updates emphasizing failures with no metrics, milestones, or asks.
The user prefers dense legal contract language with liability clauses in job postings instead of role scope and culture.
The user always chooses the cheapest offshore contractors for engineering with no timezone overlap, domain expertise, or code review standards.
The user prefers extremely long philosophical essays in company vision memos with no OKRs, priorities, or quarterly focus areas.
The user prefers deep technical architecture slides with code snippets in investor pitch decks instead of problem, market size, and traction narrative.
The user always rejects advisors, mentors, and board input for strategic decisions and relies solely on personal intuition.
The user prefers passive voice in customer apology emails after outages with no accountability, remediation steps, or compensation offer.
